claim: GAO's Dodd-Frank-mandated review (GAO-11-696, 2011) found emergency loans outstanding peaked above $1 trillion in late 2008, found no missing funds or major financial-reporting control failures, and did find insufficiently robust conflict-of-interest rules, noncompetitive emergency vendor contracts and weak documentation of atypical lending decisions. Seven recommendations issued.
falsification: Later GAO work reversing these findings

notes.ceiling: THIS IS THE DOMAIN'S STRONGEST LEGITIMATE CRITICISM AND IT IS NOT THE POPULAR ONE. Not vanished trillions - concentrated emergency discretion producing documented procurement, conflict-management and documentation weaknesses at enormous scale.
